In most situations, a therapist cannot force an adult client into eating disorder treatment against their will. Voluntary admission requires your consent, and you generally have the right to make decisions about your own care.

However, there are exceptions. If a therapist believes someone is in immediate, life-threatening danger—for example, medically unstable due to severe malnutrition, at risk of suicide, or unable to keep themselves safe—they may be able to pursue an involuntary hold or hospitalization. The specific rules depend on where you live and the laws about mental health commitments in your area, and there's usually a legal process with time limits and review.

If you're feeling worried or pressured about treatment, it can help to talk openly with your therapist about your concerns and what options feel manageable to you. And if you're ever in crisis or unsafe, please reach out to a crisis line or emergency services right away. You deserve care that respects both your safety and your voice.
